chunks: And Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Rifa'ah ibn Musa from Aban ibn Ghassan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'With what should I proclaim the Talbiyah?' He said: 'Do not say Hajj nor Umrah, but keep Mu'tah in your heart. If you catch the Imam, you are a Mutamatti', and otherwise you are a Hajj.

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ تَغْلِبَ: Aban ibn Ghassan, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.أُهِلُّ: To proclaim the Talbiyah (verbal declaration of intention for pilgrimage)
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةَ: Mu'tah, referring to the specific type of pilgrimage where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately
key_terms.حَاجًّا: Hajj, referring to the other forms of pilgrimage (Qarin or Qadhi)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: Mutamatti', one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: How should one verbally declare the intention of Hajj al-Tamattu' during the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the Shia juristic preference for 'internal intention' (Niyyah Qalbiyyah) over verbal declaration during the Talbiah, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of explicit verbalization. It underscores the flexibility in Hajj classification based on the pilgrim's arrival relative to the Imam, a key principle in Usuli fiqh regarding the validity of the Tamattu' form.
